subject: Geo-anchoring and burst window alignment for Quantico capacity
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo-anchoring and burst window alignment for Quantico capacity

Alec — quick summary and ask as we move from buying intent to activation: we want to pin the initial Dedicated GPU pools for Quantico to a primary anchor in us-west1 and a warm failover in us-east1, with cross-region burst allowed during configured business windows. Goals are predictable latency for your west-coast customers and capacity headroom for peak ETL runs.

Key asks from your side:
- Confirm primary region preference (we propose us-west1).
- Share NetOps contact for peering/VPC setup and any egress restrictions.
- Any procurement constraints on committed burst spend or daily window caps.

Attached: quantico_capacity_matrix.xlsx (proposed pool sizing by model/peak qps) and quantico_net_arch_v1.pdf (network checklist).

High-level proposal (tentative):
- Primary anchor: us-west1 (2x baseline pool, 4x burst cap)
- Warm failover: us-east1 (1x baseline, 2x burst)
- Autoscale/burst policy: enable up to 200% baseline during business hours (09:00-17:00 PT) with cooldown 10m; off-peak burst allowed up to 125% with manual approval.

Next steps: can we have NetOps contact and procurement constraints by EOD Friday? We want to schedule the initial implementation call next week to lock network and security items.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: quantico_capacity_matrix.xlsx (xlsx), quantico_net_arch_v1.pdf (pdf)

Ben — thanks, this direction looks right. A few notes from our side:
- Primary region: us-west1 is preferred (closest to our inference traffic).
- Procurement: we have a committed budget envelope but need clear daily burst caps documented in the SOW; procurement (cc'd) will confirm exact limits.
- NetOps: ping Maya Fernandez (maya@quantico.ai) for peering and firewall rules. She owns the VPN/DirectConnect setup.

From: Maya Fernandez <maya@quantico.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-anchoring and burst window alignment for Quantico capacity

Ben / Alec — Maya here, NetOps. A few gating items from networking/security to unblock region placement:
1) Peering: Quantico will require VPC peering with Redwood dedicated egress subnets for us-west1. We need CIDR ranges and proposed peering MTU.
2) Firewall: outbound egress to Redwood inference endpoints on ports 443/9443; allow health-check IPs (I can provide list).
3) Maintenance windows: we prefer cutovers outside 02:00-06:00 PT for stateful infra changes. Burst windows are fine during business hours but any cross-region cache warm-ups need scheduled notices (we want to avoid cache storms).

Please send the proposed CIDR list and the peering request template. If you can share the manifest of pool names and tags (so we can map to our routing rules) that speeds the setup.

Maya Fernandez
NetOps, Quantico AI
maya@quantico.ai
